The Sound of Music. The nineteen fifty-nine musical by Richard Rodgers, music, and Oscar Hammerstein II, lyrics, telling the true story of the von Trapp family and their escape from Nazi-occupied Austria. Centering on the romance between a free-spirited novice nun and a widowed Naval officer, it blends coming-of-age, family warmth, and historical peril into the most successful musical of all time.

This was Rodgers and Hammerstein's final and most commercially successful collaboration before Hammerstein's death. It features iconic songs including "My Favorite Things," "Do-Re-Mi," the beloved musical-education sequence, "Sixteen Going on Seventeen," and the title song "The Sound of Music." Hammerstein's last show, the opening number "The Sound of Music," sung by Maria to the nuns, was one of the last songs he wrote before his death in August nineteen sixty.

The nineteen sixty-five film adaptation, directed by Robert Wise and starring Julie Andrews, became the highest-grossing film of its era and remains the most-watched movie musical ever. The plot centers on Maria, a rebellious governess caring for the von Trapp children, seven of them, named in ascending order, and the growing romance with their father, Captain von Trapp, set against the Nazi invasion of Austria.

The show won five Tony Awards on stage in nineteen sixty. The film won ten Academy Awards, including Best Picture, and dominated the global box office for over a decade. The closing scene, the family's escape over the Alps into Switzerland, transcends the musical-theatre medium into pure cinematic symbol of freedom.
